rows: A diagnostic paragraph identifies a claim but provides no quotation. Which revision best establishes a reading baseline?
Add a specific detail from the passage and explain how it supports the claim.
Replace the claim with a longer personal opinion.
Add two unrelated vocabulary words.
Keep the paragraph unchanged to preserve a clean first draft.
A baseline captures actual evidence-based reasoning rather than presentation alone.
Baseline reading
A learner writes, 'The evidence is clear the argument is incomplete.' Which revision correctly separates the complete clauses?
The evidence is clear; the argument is incomplete.
The evidence is clear, the argument is incomplete.
The evidence is clear the argument, is incomplete.
The evidence is clear. Because the argument incomplete.
A semicolon correctly joins two related independent clauses.
Sentence boundaries
A map labels three roads, but its legend omits the scale. Which inference can the reader defend?
The map shows a route but does not establish the distances involved.
The shortest-looking road must be the fastest.
The map proves which road travelers prefer.
A missing scale means the route never existed.
The visual supports route relationships, not unsupported physical distances.
Evidence limitation
A student writes, 'The annotation identifies a detail it does not yet explain its significance.' Which revision clarifies the relationship?
The annotation identifies a detail, but it does not yet explain its significance.
The annotation identifies a detail, it does not yet explain its significance.
The annotation identifies. A detail it does not yet explain.
The annotation identifies a detail but, it does not yet explain its significance.
The coordinating conjunction but joins the contrasting complete clauses when preceded by a comma.
Clause connection
A summary repeats a source's unusual sentence pattern with only two synonyms changed. What makes it academically weak?
It retains the source's phrasing structure without a genuinely independent paraphrase.
It removes too many claims from the source.
It uses fewer sentences than the original.
It introduces a new but supported interpretation.
Accurate paraphrase needs independent language and attribution, not cosmetic substitutions.
Academic integrity
Which attribution is clearest when a paragraph changes from a source's claim to the student's inference?
'The author reports the decline; this pattern may suggest a second cause.'
'Everyone knows the decline proves the cause.'
'The decline was real, obviously, and no citation is needed.'
'The author reports it and that settles every possible question.'
A source report and an independent inference are distinguished and qualified.
Source attribution
A narrator notices the empty storefront but not the crowded shelter nearby. What is the strongest interpretation?
The narrator's limited attention shapes the setting readers can reconstruct.
The shelter must be abandoned.
The author necessarily endorses the narrator's judgment.
The storefront proves the plot takes place in winter.
Point of view constrains available information without proving unseen events.
Narrative perspective
Which sentence uses an appositive to identify a speaker without changing the factual claim?
Mira, the town archivist, presented the letter.
Mira the town archivist presented, the letter.
Mira, presented the town archivist the letter.
Mira the town, archivist presented the letter.
The phrase between commas renames Mira without splitting the core clause.
Appositive punctuation
A teenager hides an unfinished application after being praised for independence. Which evidence best supports an internal conflict?
The contrast between public praise and the concealed unfinished form.
The number of other students in the school.
The application paper's color.
An unrelated description of the weather.
Character motivation emerges from tension between expectation and behavior.
Characterization
Which revision maintains a consistent past-time account?
She mailed the draft after she revised the ending.
She mails the draft after she revised the ending.
She had mailed the draft before she will revise it.
She mail the draft after she revises the ending yesterday.
Both completed narrative actions are expressed in a coherent past tense.
Tense control
Two narrators describe one protest: one emphasizes traffic; the other, access for workers. Which comparison is justified?
Their positions direct attention to different consequences of the same event.
One narrator must have fabricated the entire event.
Both narrators express identical priorities.
The second narrator describes a separate protest.
Different focal points need not mean entirely incompatible facts.
Perspective comparison
Which parallel revision most clearly contrasts the narrators?
One describes delays; the other describes unequal access.
One describing delays; the other describes unequal access.
One describes delays; the other describing unequal access.
One describes delays, and unequal access described by the other.
Matching finite-verb structures helps readers compare equivalent actions.
Parallel structure
Two tales portray generosity: one through a small gift and one through refusing a reward. What is a thematic comparison?
Both test what generosity requires, using contrasting choices to develop the idea.
Both contain exactly the same plot events.
Both belong to the same culture because of the theme.
The only theme is that gifts always solve conflict.
A shared concern can develop differently through character decisions.
Cross-text theme
Which thesis uses parallel comparison and avoids equating unlike plots?
Although the actions differ, both stories question the value of self-interest.
The stories are both generosity, and also reward.
Story one a gift, story two refuses.
Both stories prove every generous character is rewarded.
The concessive clause establishes contrast while the main clause states a defensible common theme.
Comparative thesis
A passage shifts from clipped commands to reflective long sentences. Which reading examines style rather than just plot?
The change in sentence rhythm may signal a move from urgency to reflection.
The first sentences must be written by another author.
Short sentences make all characters dishonest.
The passage has no tone because sentence lengths vary.
Sentence design can affect pacing and perceived voice.
Syntax and tone
Which punctuation best creates a deliberate, immediate interruption?
'I thought the door was open—until I saw the lock.'
'I thought, the door was open until I saw the lock.'
'I thought the door was open until, I saw the lock.'
'I thought the door was open; until I saw the lock.'
A dash can mark the sudden reversal without creating a sentence fragment.
Punctuation for effect
A literary essay cites a character's refusal but calls it 'courage' without explanation. What is missing?
Commentary connecting the action to a defensible interpretation of courage.
An extra plot summary with no claim.
Three synonyms for the word courageous.
A statement that no counterreading is possible.
A quotation does not interpret itself; reasoning links evidence to thesis.
Analytical commentary
Which sentence integrates a brief quotation grammatically?
The narrator calls the decision 'necessary,' a word that minimizes its cost.
The narrator calls: 'necessary' the decision and its cost.
The narrator, calls the decision 'necessary' a word.
The narrator 'necessary' calls and minimizes.
A complete clause embeds the quotation and then comments on diction.
Quote integration
A speech begins with a local problem, then expands to a national claim. What structural effect can this create?
The concrete opening supplies an example before the argument broadens.
The speaker abandons the subject without any connection.
The speech becomes a poem automatically.
The wider claim is proven solely by its later placement.
A specific-to-general progression can organize reasoning but does not guarantee its validity.
Rhetorical structure
Which sentence correctly joins two related independent historical claims?
The petition preceded the speech; the response came later.
The petition preceded the speech, the response came later.
The petition preceded; the speech the response came later.
The petition preceded the speech: because the response came later.
A semicolon links closely related independent clauses without a comma splice.
Semicolon logic
An advocate addresses an audience that distrusts official numbers. Which rhetorical choice best responds to that concern?
Explain the data source, limitations, and method before drawing conclusions.
Repeat a statistic more loudly instead of citing it.
Assume that all listeners share the same experience.
Remove qualifiers to make the claim appear certain.
Audience awareness shapes what evidence and explanation an argument needs.
Audience and credibility
Which revision turns repetition into a purposeful appeal?
'We need clear records. We need fair access. We need answers.'
'We need clear records. The access of fairness. Need answers we.'
'Clear records, fair access, answers; the we need.'
'We need we need, clear records because fair access.'
Repetition of the grammatical opening gives the three demands rhythmic emphasis.
Anaphora
A speech repeats 'not for a few, but for all' three times. Which analysis names the device and its effect?
Repetition reinforces an inclusive contrast central to the argument.
The statement is a factual proof of universal access.
Repetition removes the need for audience analysis.
The phrase introduces an unrelated plot twist.
Repeated antithetical phrasing can focus an audience on the key contrast.
Rhetorical repetition
Which revision makes the parallel structure more consistent?
The policy aims to inform residents, protect workers, and serve families.
The policy aims informing residents, to protect workers, and service families.
The policy aims to inform residents, workers protecting, and families.
The policy aims informing residents, protect workers, and to serve families.
Three infinitive verb phrases provide consistent syntactic emphasis.
Parallel clauses
Two articles disagree about whether a schedule reduced congestion. What should a fair comparison examine first?
Their definitions of congestion, evidence periods, and methods.
Which article has the more forceful headline.
Which writer agrees with the student's first opinion.
Whether one article includes more adjectives.
Validity depends on comparable definitions and methods, not rhetoric alone.
Argument validity
Which qualified sentence reports an uncertain cause fairly?
'The timing is consistent with a possible effect, but other factors remain untested.'
'The new plan certainly caused every change.'
'Because traffic changed, no other variable matters.'
'The headline alone settles the issue.'
Qualified causal language acknowledges what observational timing cannot establish.
Causal qualification
An opposing writer accepts the data but disputes a policy's fairness. Which counterargument would be intellectually fair?
Represent the fairness concern accurately before assessing its evidence and assumptions.
Call the opponent ignorant without stating the argument.
Claim the opponent rejects the data when they do not.
Ignore the moral criterion because numbers are available.
Counterargument should address the actual claim rather than misrepresent it.
Rebuttal accuracy
Which concession strengthens rather than abandons an argument?
'Although costs may rise initially, the proposed schedule could improve access.'
'My opponents are confused, so their concern is irrelevant.'
'Costs rise; therefore no analysis is necessary.'
'Although costs, schedule could improve.'
The concession acknowledges a real difficulty while preserving a qualified claim.
Concession syntax
During debate, a classmate identifies an error in a statistic. What is the strongest immediate response?
Acknowledge and correct the figure before continuing the argument.
Repeat the incorrect number with more confidence.
Attack the questioner's speaking style.
Change topics without addressing the challenged claim.
Responsible oral argument corrects material inaccuracies openly.
Debate ethics
Which oral transition signals a response to another position?
'That objection raises a fair concern; here is the evidence I would examine.'
'Anyway, you obviously cannot follow this.'
'The next point is my favorite.'
'We can skip that because time is moving.'
The opening fairly acknowledges the counterpoint and introduces evidence.
Responsive discourse
Three reports supply a timeline, interviews, and a chart. What does real synthesis do?
Explain how the different forms of evidence qualify or reinforce one conclusion.
Describe each source in isolation without relationships.
Treat interview opinion as automatically equal to measured totals.
Copy each report's introduction as separate paragraphs.
Synthesis connects sources and weighs their differing evidentiary roles.
Expository synthesis
Which integrated sentence clearly distinguishes sources?
'The timeline locates the change, while the chart estimates its size.'
'Timeline change, chart size, and therefore truth.'
'Because the timeline, the chart estimates.'
'The timeline locates, while the chart it estimates.'
Parallel clauses contrast the distinct functions of each evidence type.
Source comparison
An essay's pronouns shift between 'they' for two different groups. Which revision should come first?
Replace ambiguous pronouns with specific nouns where reference is unclear.
Insert more pronouns to keep the prose short.
Change all verbs to passive voice regardless of meaning.
Delete evidence that names either group.
Readers must know which group each claim describes.
Pronoun reference
Which sentence has clear subject–verb agreement?
'Each of the revised paragraphs contains an explicit claim.'
'Each of the revised paragraphs contain an explicit claim.'
'Each of the revised paragraphs containing an explicit claim.'
'Each of the revised paragraphs have containing an explicit claim.'
The singular subject each requires contains.
Agreement
A learner scores poorly on inference but well on identifying details. Which review is most targeted?
Practice linking quoted details to explanations of implied meaning.
Spend all review time memorizing author birth dates.
Retake only vocabulary questions already mastered.
Replace the evidence notebook with a score list.
The targeted gap concerns reasoning from evidence, not detail recognition.
Midterm diagnostic
Which revision memo documents a real correction?
'I confused the speaker with the author; I rechecked pronouns and revised the claim.'
'The essay is better now because I changed the font.'
'I did not revise anything but the score should rise.'
'I removed sources because they complicated my position.'
An effective memo names the original error, the evidence checked, and the correction.
Metacognitive revision
A poem's speaker refers to 'my return' but the poet lived elsewhere. Which claim is safest?
The speaker may be a constructed voice; biographical identity needs separate evidence.
The speaker is always the historical poet.
The poem must be fictional because of the difference.
The poet's biography makes the line meaningless.
Lyric voice and the historical author should not be conflated.
Poetic speaker
Which sentence qualifies an interpretation of ambiguity?
'The image may suggest relief, although its context also supports grief.'
'The image can only mean relief, regardless of context.'
'Every reader's claim is equally supported by the words.'
'The author certainly felt relief because of the image.'
A qualified interpretation identifies textual alternatives without claiming the author's emotions.
Poetic qualification
A poem calls the corridor 'cold' despite describing summer weather. What should the reader investigate?
Whether cold conveys emotional distance rather than literal temperature.
Whether summer always includes ice.
Whether the poem's speaker is a thermometer.
Whether every adjective is factually measurable.
Connotation permits emotional associations beyond literal weather.
Connotation
Which revision uses a precise image-rich verb?
'Light fractured across the scratched glass.'
'Light was a thing across the glass.'
'Light did a movement kind of across glass.'
'Light was basically something on glass.'
Fractured suggests the appearance of divided light more precisely than vague filler.
Imagery diction
Two poems repeat the same phrase, but one places it before a turn and the other after. What matters analytically?
The position of the repetition within each poem's change in argument or emotion.
The fact that both have exactly the same meaning.
Whether either poem contains a character named Turn.
The number of pages in their publishers' catalogs.
Formal position shapes the rhetorical role of repetition.
Poetic structure
Which comparative sentence integrates two works without flattening them?
'Both poems repeat the phrase, yet its placement changes the emphasis.'
'Both poems repeat the phrase and have identical meanings.'
'Both poems repeat, their placements changes meaning.'
'Both poems repetition, although its placement.'
The sentence establishes a similarity and an interpretable structural difference.
Comparative grammar
A myth recurs in two cultures with different choices and consequences. What should comparative analysis avoid?
Assuming a shared figure establishes a single identical cultural value.
Examining the distinct narrative settings.
Comparing the effects of character choices.
Identifying the evidence that supports each reading.
Shared motifs can be shaped by different traditions and contexts.
Myth comparison
Which sentence introduces an allusion clearly?
'The narrator invokes a familiar journey motif to frame the difficult choice.'
'The narrator journeys motif, to frame familiar choice.'
'A journey motif invoked narrator familiar choice.'
'The narrator, invokes a familiar journey motif, to frame the choice.'
The allusion is integrated into a complete interpretive statement.
Allusion integration
When comparing a sacred narrative with its literary adaptation, what is the most responsible task?
Analyze narrative techniques and context without evaluating people's beliefs as literature scores.
Assume all adherents interpret the passage identically.
Declare one tradition's moral claims objectively superior.
Treat every adaptation as a verbatim translation.
Literary analysis can be rigorous and respectful without pronouncing on faith commitments.
Respectful literary analysis
Which attribution best separates text and interpretation?
'In the selected narrative, the speaker says X; the adaptation shifts the emphasis to Y.'
'Every community believes the adaptation replaces the original.'
'The narrative means Y for all readers without exception.'
'The adaptation is wrong because it differs.'
The sentence identifies textual choices without universalizing readers' convictions.
Contextual attribution
A film omits a novel's interior monologue but adds a silent close-up. Which claim analyzes medium?
The close-up may convey emotion visually where prose supplied internal thought.
The filmmaker necessarily misunderstood the novel.
The omitted monologue proves film cannot carry meaning.
The camera choice guarantees the audience interprets one emotion.
Medium-specific techniques change how information is communicated.
Adaptation methods
Which comparative thesis is defensible?
'The adaptation replaces narrated thought with visual emphasis, changing the audience's access to motive.'
'The adaptation is a film and the novel is a book.'
'The adaptation is better because the camera is close.'
'The writer used thoughts, which the film did not and therefore proves nothing.'
The claim interprets a consequential change rather than listing formats.
Comparative argument
A student wants to study 'the history of everything people read.' Which question is most researchable?
'How did one town library's teen lending change over five recorded years?'
'Why has every reader always liked stories?'
'Is reading good for all people everywhere?'
'Which book is objectively best across every era?'
A bounded population, variable, and time frame permit feasible evidence collection.
Inquiry scope
Which proposal sentence names a measurable scope?
'I will analyze public circulation totals from 2020–2024 for this library.'
'I will prove that all libraries changed forever.'
'I will research books a lot and hopefully find things.'
'I will compare everything readers have ever published.'
Specific years, source type, and institution set practical limits.
Research syntax
An online page cites a study but has no link to the original method. What is the best next step?
Locate the study and verify its sampling and reported findings.
Trust the claim because the page uses an official-looking logo.
Reject the study solely because it disagrees with a blog.
Use only the page's headline as supporting evidence.
Lateral reading requires tracing a claim beyond the surface that repeats it.
Source verification
Which evaluation sentence uses justified uncertainty?
'The claim is plausible, but the sample description remains unverified.'
'The claim must be right because it has a chart.'
'The claim is certainly wrong because the sample is not listed here.'
'The claim is proven without looking at its source.'
The sentence limits confidence to what source information supports.
Evaluation qualifier
Notes reproduce a source's distinctive phrase without quotation marks. What should the researcher repair?
Mark exact borrowed words and retain enough citation information to find the source.
Change one adjective and call it original work.
Erase the source identity from the notes.
Assume research notes are exempt from ethical attribution.
Quotation boundaries and source metadata prevent later accidental patchwriting.
Research source ethics
Which signal phrase correctly attributes a source rather than a student's inference?
'According to the report, attendance increased; the cause remains uncertain.'
'Attendance increased because the report says it did, undoubtedly.'
'Everyone knows attendance increased and what caused it.'
'The report increased, attendance because of it.'
Clear attribution separates the observed claim from a qualified causal inference.
Signal phrase
A research report lists facts but never explains why they relate. What change improves exposition?
Organize sections around a controlling idea and explain relationships between the findings.
Add more disconnected quotations.
Replace all headings with decorative labels.
Move every source citation to the title.
Expository coherence requires explanation, not an inventory of details.
Expository reasoning
Which transition identifies a relationship without overstating causality?
'Similarly, both reports describe increased participation, though they measure different groups.'
'Therefore, the first report caused the second.'
'The reports both participate, moreover groups.'
'The reports agree completely, so methods do not matter.'
Similarity is qualified by the difference in sampled populations.
Expository transitions
A policy writer reports a correlation but calls it proof that the proposal works. What is the best repair?
Limit the claim to the observed association and examine competing explanations.
Delete the table but retain the causal claim.
Insist that correlation establishes causation.
Add emotional adjectives instead of evaluating methods.
Causal conclusions require design and reasoning beyond association.
Argument evidence
Which sentence concedes a limitation without abandoning the proposal?
'Although the survey is small, its responses identify concerns worth testing further.'
'The survey is small, so its respondents do not exist.'
'The survey is small; therefore the policy always fails.'
'Although survey small respondents, concerns worth.'
The concession accurately narrows the inference while preserving the relevance of observed concerns.
Research concession
A student makes a chart's axis begin at 95 to exaggerate a small change. What ethical correction is needed?
State the axis choice clearly and use a scale that does not conceal the practical size of the change.
Hide the axis labels to keep the design clean.
Change the source numbers to fit a dramatic headline.
Remove any citation for the underlying values.
Visual scales can distort magnitude without changing raw data.
Digital publication ethics
Which caption lets readers interpret a chart independently?
'Weekly visits, 2023–2024; source: municipal report; vertical axis starts at zero.'
'A shocking graph proves everything.'
'Visits went up because the colors are bold.'
'Numbers and lines appear in this image.'
An informative caption provides measure, period, source, and scale context.
Accessible caption
An audience knows one character's secret while another character does not. What dramatic effect can follow?
The audience can interpret apparently ordinary dialogue with dramatic irony.
The scene cannot contain conflict.
All actors must speak directly to the audience.
The concealed information makes stage directions unnecessary.
A gap between audience and character knowledge creates dramatic irony.
Dramatic irony
Which punctuation best marks a brief interrupted exchange?
'“Wait—” “The door is already shut,” she replied.'
'“Wait,” “The door is already shut,” she replied.'
'“Wait;” “The door is already shut,” she replied.'
'“Wait:” “The door is already shut,” she replied.'
The dash indicates an interruption before the second speaker's reply.
Dialogue punctuation
A Shakespearean character uses an unfamiliar word order. What reading strategy is strongest?
Identify the subject and verb, then paraphrase while checking imagery and context.
Replace every unusual phrase with a modern slogan.
Ignore the line because its syntax is old.
Assume inverted syntax always expresses sarcasm.
Grammatical reconstruction should preserve meaning and poetic choices.
Early modern syntax
Which performance note is precise without pretending to know the author's one intended delivery?
'Pause after the question to foreground the speaker's uncertainty.'
'Say everything loudly because Shakespeare wrote it.'
'Ignore punctuation because actors must improvise.'
'Pause randomly without reference to meaning.'
A specific textual feature motivates the interpretive performance choice.
Performance annotation
A director changes the timing of a pause. What evidence could justify this interpretive choice?
The pause highlights a shift in the character's motive visible in adjacent lines.
The pause makes the scene automatically historically accurate.
All performances must use identical pauses.
The director should conceal textual reasons from the cast.
Performance interpretation should connect craft decisions to the script.
Dramatic interpretation
Which reflection is evidence-based?
'I delayed the reply to expose the hesitation suggested by the line.'
'The scene improved because I preferred my own interpretation.'
'Any pause proves the character was frightened.'
'The text did not matter to my staging choices.'
The reflection names a choice and links it to a textual reason.
Performance reflection
Across chapters, an image of locked doors recurs when characters withhold information. What is the best motif claim?
The image may develop a pattern connecting secrecy with restricted agency.
Every locked door always symbolizes death.
Repeated images cannot contribute to theme.
The novel's publication date alone defines the motif.
Recurring details gain interpretive force from patterned contexts.
Long-form motif
Which notebook entry helps track motif development?
'Ch. 2: locked door after refusal; Ch. 8: locked door before confession; possible change in meaning.'
'Locked doors seem important, no chapters needed.'
'Doors appear; the novel must have one theme.'
'I remember a door and therefore know the ending.'
Specific chapter locations and changing contexts support sustained analysis.
Chapter evidence tracking
A portfolio includes a polished final essay but no drafts. What evidence would better demonstrate growth?
An earlier annotated draft plus targeted revisions and a reflection on why they mattered.
A larger decorative cover image.
More copies of the finished essay.
An undated score without the work.
Process evidence shows the change in skill over time.
Portfolio evidence
Which conference statement supports a claim of improvement?
'My later analysis integrates evidence more precisely; these two drafts show the change.'
'I improved because the second essay is longer.'
'I grew because no one challenged my interpretation.'
'All my work is perfect, so feedback is irrelevant.'
A comparison of two artifacts supports a specific development claim.
Evidence-based reflection
A student has mastered locating claims but misses causal reasoning questions. What is an effective final review?
Practice distinguishing observed relationships from supported explanations in new passages.
Repeat only previously correct claim-location problems.
Replace all test preparation with memorizing quotes.
Avoid looking at feedback until after the exam.
Targeted transfer addresses the specific reasoning gap.
Final review
Which post-course goal is measurable?
'For three weeks I will annotate evidence and explain one inference from each new article.'
'I will always become better at reading.'
'I will use difficult words in every sentence.'
'I will never make an interpretive mistake.'
The goal defines frequency, task, and an observable reasoning product.
Goal-setting
